row.reason: a row shard begins mid-column, so it carries an INITIAL_STATE plane, and the span-2 TCQ decoders this family's route packs for (tessera.lane_planes.pack_unit_for_kernel, csrc/window_gemv.cu) supply state_{-1} = 0 themselves; the loader refuses such a cut on EVERY rank, including rank 0 whose shard would pack, because a group whose ranks disagree about a module hangs on its first collective

tensor_parallel.units_note: max_world_size is an ATTESTATION bound: the largest tensor-parallel world size a served receipt covers. It is 1 for every declared family because no multi-rank serve has been run. loader_axes is a different claim -- what this build's LOADER does with each shard axis -- and it is checked against tessera.serving.sharding.ROUTE_TP_AXES, which the routes gate on, so the document and the code cannot drift. A serve above max_world_size is unattested, which is the same honest status a rung with no lane_eligibility cell has, and not a refusal.

fused_module.fields_note: Inside one vLLM-fused module (q/k/v, gate/up), what every role must SHARE and what is free PER MEMBER. vLLM builds one quant method per module, so the family -- and with it the grid, body, scale plane and input width the route decodes to one tile -- is a module fact. The RATE is not: every decoder in this build reads each role from that role's OWN manifest (fp8_route/bf16_route call prepare_window on unit.body_bits/unit.rates/unit.window_bits per role and concatenate; nvfp4_route packs each role's own rate/arity/memory/half scalars and decodes into that role's row slice). This block is checked against tessera.serving.scheme.FUSED_MODULE_FIELDS, the dict the loader itself gates on, exactly as tensor_parallel.units[].loader_axes is checked against sharding.ROUTE_TP_AXES.
fused_module.sidecar_q256_note: How a fused module's rungs are spelled in the checkpoint's scheme. ONE field, one fact: config_groups[..].scheme.q256 is an integer when every role carries the same rung -- the spelling of every checkpoint written before contract v6, unchanged -- or a list of one integer per role, in the scheme's own roles order, when they differ. A plugin build older than v6 refuses the list form on sight ('q256 must be an integer'), which is the fail-closed direction; a v6 build reads both.
fused_module.mixed_rung_receipt_note: Whether a CONTAINER RECEIPT covers a served module whose members took different rungs. It is false: the relaxation is proven by a decode identity (a real Qwen3-0.6B q/k/v at three rungs decodes element-for-element to what the three roles decode alone -- experiments/fused_member_rung_identity.py, tests/test_fused_member_rungs.py), not by a vLLM serve. This is the same distinction loader_axes draws against max_world_size: what the loader accepts is not what a receipt has covered. lane_eligibility is UNCHANGED by this version, so a mixed-rung module's cells resolve exactly as its members' rungs do individually -- unattested where no cell names the rung, which is the honest status and not a refusal.

construction.note: Which Linears the pinned runtime OFFERS to a quant config, per architecture. LinearBase.__init__ takes UnquantizedLinearMethod() in the quant_config is None branch WITHOUT calling get_quant_method, so a model that builds a projection with quant_config=None takes vLLM's own BF16 method and this plugin is never asked -- it cannot refuse, warn, or see the prefix. A wire written there deletes the <module>.weight the runtime wants and puts bytes in its place that nothing decodes. offered/never_offered are vLLM MODULE patterns with repeat indices collapsed to '*'; a producer translates its checkpoint names with hf_to_vllm_mapper_unstacked first (the same table configure_quant_config hands this plugin) and normalises the same way. A name in neither list is a module the runtime does not build. Every row is DERIVED from a receipt under docs/measurements/construction/ by contract.construction_entry_from_receipt and re-derived in tests/test_serving_construction.py, so the table cannot drift from the observation; the observation itself is tools/tessera_construction_census.py, which builds the model the way the loader does and records every prefix a probe quant config is offered. An architecture with no row is UNCENSUSED, which is an honest gap and not a claim that everything is routed.

changelog.change: Lane-eligibility schema v8 (#198), pre-release evidence correction: evidence.artifact is required and is null when no encoder-reproduction comparison is recorded. Otherwise it names the historical artifact and full encoder commit, plus the exact re-encode commit, single unit, payload relation, weight_sse relation and receipt. The four dense E4M3 cells name the checkpoint built at 8070ec6; a same-source down_proj comparison at 3317036 (also measured before wire minor 7 at 1e58fdc) finds a different payload and slightly lower weight SSE. This is a single-unit screen, not served KL, whole-model quality evidence or a claim about a future encoder. It never changes grade or the historical KL entries. The closed validator rejects malformed or inconsistent scope. Rungs, routes, launches, serving defaults, wire bytes and encoder behavior do not change. This schema has no released consumers; no migration shim is provided.

Lane-eligibility schema v7 (#195): a greedy smoke names the CONTROL it was compared against, so a consumer can tell "this route degenerates" from "this prompt degenerates on this model". WHAT WAS WRONG: both routed_moe cells published smoke.status 'repetitive', an accurate record of what came back, and a producer-side gate refused the whole routed-MoE lane on it -- correctly under the rule it was given, because principle 9 requires a route to generate correctly. Then the control was run: the same prompt, byte for byte from experiments/tessera_plugin_served.sh, against the BF16 SOURCE on the same pinned image, eager, returns ' France is France is ...' character for character identical to the Tessera student's (docs/measurements/moe-evidence-debt-2026-09-04.md section 7). The repetition is the model and the prompt, not the quantisation -- and that fact lived in prose while the field a gate reads said 'repetitive'. A machine-readable value true about the observation and misleading about its meaning, with the disambiguating measurement unreadable by any consumer, is principle 14 one level up, which is why the fix is in the schema and not in either consumer. WHAT THE FIELD IS: smoke gains control, either null or the closed {reference, outcome, receipt} -- reference from contract.EVIDENCE_CONTROL_REFERENCES ('bf16_source', the unquantised source the route is a quantisation of), outcome from EVIDENCE_CONTROL_OUTCOMES, receipt a repository path under docs/measurements/ like every other receipt here (grammar in the validator, existence in a tree test). WHAT OUTCOME ESTABLISHES, EXACTLY: 'identical_completion' means the reference returned the SAME completion for the same prompt under the smoke's own runtime and execution mode; 'different_completion' means the completions differ -- NOT that the reference was healthy, which no string comparison can decide. WHAT A CONSUMER READS: attribution, DERIVED from control and checked, exactly as grade is derived from kl -- no control 'unattributed' (nobody ran the reference, so the status is an observation and not an attribution), 'identical_completion' 'shared_with_reference', 'different_completion' 'not_shared_with_reference' (weaker than 'the route is at fault', and deliberately not spelled that way). A gate that refused on status alone now refuses on status 'repetitive' AND attribution other than 'shared_with_reference', which is the pair that carries the decision. NO scope FIELD: a smoke record carries no scope of its own, a control cannot be better scoped than the thing it controls, and that the arms match is what the receipt attests -- as for every other receipt-backed field here. ONE control and not a list, deliberately: one is what has been run, and a second reference is a bump rather than a surprise. WHAT MOVED ON THE TABLE: the two routed_moe cells carry the control above and read shared_with_reference; the eight dense cells carry control null and attribution 'unattributed' -- six of them never ran a smoke and the two BF16 cells ran one with no reference arm. No status word changed: 'repetitive' is still what came back. No rung, route, activation contract, launch, grade, KL entry, qualification, TP/EP bound or byte moved. NOT ADDITIVE, and the schema string says so: a v6 reader must not read a v7 document, both because attribution and control are keys its closed smoke object does not know and because -- the reason the version exists -- a v6 reader goes on making a decision off status that status no longer carries alone. The same release also corrected the three build-box absolute paths in this changelog's own prose (#181, contract v17, prose-only and unversioned); this entry is the schema half.

Lane-eligibility schema v6 (#131, #133): a cell names its own evidence instead of borrowing a global. (1) versions.attested_on is REMOVED. It did double duty -- the toolchain the contract was written against and the runtime the cells were measured on -- and was false for the two routed_moe cells, which were measured on eugr/spark-vllm@sha256:0afec8d4... under vLLM 0.28.1rc1.dev397+gfd4a15126.d20260904, not vllm/vllm-openai under 0.28.0. Each cell's runtime now carries the vllm and torch build its OWN receipt records (dense: 0.28.0 / 2.13.0+cu130 per tessera-window-gemv-served-2026-09-03.md and tessera-bf16-route-served-2026-09-02.md; routed_moe: the census receipt docs/measurements/census/lfm25-8b-a1b-served-r4.json versions block), beside the v5 image and execution_modes scope; the validator requires all four and refuses two toolchains under one digest. versions is now closed to {tessera, plugin_entry_point, default_serve_image} and every field is checked: tessera non-empty, plugin_entry_point the one this package registers, default_serve_image an exact digest that some cell attests. default_serve_image is the serve-image pin harnesses read (runtime_image.PIN_CONTRACT_FIELD, previously versions.attested_on.image); its value is the dense cells' image and did not move. The old device field is dropped: platform and compute_capability already carry it. (2) Every cell carries a required, closed evidence object {grade, kl[], smoke} so a gate can read what grade of evidence the cell rests on, never prose. PREMISE CORRECTION recorded here because it decides the values: every served KL this repository holds, dense and MoE alike, is a kl_tool top-1024 teacher/student-intersection LOWER BOUND, so no cell grades kl_full_vocab and 'the MoE cells carry screen-grade evidence while the dense cells do not' is not the distinction. The distinctions are which REGIME the bound was scored in, under which execution modes, whether a greedy smoke is on record, and the population (one Qwen3-0.6B artifact per dense family; one LFM2.5-8B-A1B artifact for routed_moe). A kl entry is {kind, top_k, regime, execution_modes, receipt}; regime must be the cell's own (a prefill bound written into a decode cell is refused), execution_modes a subset of the cell's, receipt a repository path under docs/measurements/ (existence is a tree test). smoke is {status in recorded|repetitive|not_recorded, receipt}. grade is DERIVED from the entries (route_only when no bound in the cell's regime; kl_lower_bound; kl_full_vocab) and checked, like executes. Resulting grades: batch cells all kl_lower_bound (E2M1 and E4M3-resident from tessera-serving-plugin-2026-09-02.md eager+compiled; E4M3-streamed from tessera-window-gemv-served-2026-09-03.md arm A eager+compiled; BF16 from its receipt, eager; routed_moe from tessera-lfm-campaign-2026-09-04.md section 8, eager). Decode cells: only tessera_e4m3_k1_dense_sm121_decode_streamed has a decode-regime bound (tessera-decode-regime-kl-2026-09-03.md eager arm A; tessera-compiled-decode-kl-r6-2026-09-04.md compiled A1/A2); every other decode cell, dense and MoE, is route_only -- the census attests dispatch and nothing attests decode-regime quality. Smoke: BF16 cells recorded (identical greedy continuation, ungraded), routed_moe cells repetitive, all others not_recorded. NOT additive: a v5 reader must not read a v6 document (new required cell keys, versions renamed). No rung, route, activation contract, launch, TP/EP bound or byte moved; the eight dense cells and two routed_moe cells keep their ids and scopes. qualification is unchanged and deliberately not overloaded with the grade; whether route_only routed_moe cells should remain device_qualified is #133's open decision.

Two scoped routed_moe E4M3/q1024 resident eager sm121 cells, from the complete LFM2.5-8B-A1B artifact and exact EUGR digest. The full 22-stack/2112-projection census observed the modular TRITON FP8 route in decode M1 and prefill M64; the source-bound usable BF16 teacher/student comparison covers 4096 prefill positions, top-K1024 KL lower bound0.0831613565 and top1 agreement85.1074% (not full-vocabulary KL or decode-quality evidence). Exact artifact, runtime, source, tail limitations and cleanup receipts: docs/measurements/tessera-lfm-campaign-2026-09-04.md sections7-8. Launches derive from the existing structure-aware ROUTE_LAUNCHES. Lane schema stays v5; all eight dense cells, their default image, encoder bytes, rungs and TP/EP bounds remain unchanged. No compiled or streamed MoE claim is added.

lane_eligibility v5 requires an explicit runtime scope on each cell: exact image manifest digest and measured execution_modes. The eight existing dense cells preserve their eager and compiled scope on the existing vLLM 0.28.0 digest; versions.attested_on and all wire, activation, launch, residency, rung, TP and EP claims remain unchanged. Their historical census headers and the contemporaneous global image attestation supply that migration evidence, not newly fabricated per-census image stamps (docs/measurements/runtime-scope-migration-2026-09-04.md). Cell lookup and overlap include image and execution mode; missing runtime context resolves unattested. Existing ids remain stable, with an optional canonical-runtime hash suffix for disjoint variants and unique ids required. Old v4 readers must refuse this schema because ignoring runtime scope would widen the attestation. No routed-MoE cell is added by this schema change.

native_extensions[tessera_window_gemv].routes gains TESSERA_BF16. The window GEMV is loaded by BOTH window routes -- bf16_route.prepare_bf16_gemv repacks through kernel_window_gemv.prepare_value_unit exactly as fp8_gemv does, sets the same layer.tessera_gemv, and bf16_route.apply branches on it -- and the table said TESSERA_FP8 alone. That is a claim about this runtime narrower than the runtime: a consumer keying reproducibility on native-extension residency (PrismaQuant's serve fingerprint, which is why this block exists) would have read a BF16 serve with the extension and one without as the same serve, and they execute different launches. Found by the tie tests added with lane_eligibility v4: scheme.ROUTE_LAUNCHES gives the 16-bit route the same three launches the 8-bit one has, and test_the_launch_tables_lane_is_the_published_extension asserts every launch's lane names an extension that lists that route. The correction is also load-bearing for v4's own derivation: contract._lanes_a_rung_reaches filters candidate lanes by route, so with the narrower list a TESSERA_BF16_K1 cell could never derive a GEMV launch -- correct today only because the attested rung 1792 is root 7 and unreachable anyway, and silently wrong the day a reachable BF16 rung is attested. NO CELL MOVES: at 1792 the derivation still returns torch.mm over torch_window, because the rung, not the route list, is what refuses the lane there. loaded_by stays tessera.serving.fp8_gemv: the field is a single string by schema and both reaching modules are under tessera.serving, so it still says what it is for -- that this entry is serving-side and not producer-side -- while naming one of the two. Widening it to a list is a shape change to native_extensions with its own consumer coordination and is not attempted here. ADDITIVE for a reader that treats routes as a set: nothing was removed.

lane_eligibility schema v4: every cell publishes `executes`, the (symbol, decoder) launches the route MAKES in that cell's regime at that cell's residency on that cell's rungs -- and the E4M3 family's cells split along the residency, because that is the axis those launches differ on. WHAT WAS WRONG: a cell said which A-side contract ran (correct, and still does: the FP8 route's per-token quantiser runs on every path and hands the GEMV dequantised values, so fp8_per_token_dynamic is what executes in both regimes) and which rungs a receipt covered, and the only place the LAUNCH appeared was the cell's id -- `..._decode_scaled_mm_w8a8`, a string no gate parses. That was accidentally true while the window-GEMV lane was unreachable: every allocated checkpoint carried a rate outside kernel_window_gemv.SUPPORTED_RATES, so an E4M3 decode really did execute the materialised FP8 pair (issue #104). It stopped being true on a rate-constrained Qwen3-0.6B build, uniform q256 1024 (root rate 4 exactly), whose served census records decode: symbol tessera_window_gemv::gemv, decoder window_gemv, 112 of 112 modules; prefill: symbol torch._scaled_mm, decoder window_gemv, 112 of 112 (streamed, eager; receipt docs/measurements/tessera-gemv-lane-reachable-2026-09-03.md, which carries both census rows in section (b) and the experiments/ts104_gemv_census.sh command that produced them -- the census JSON itself is a build-box run log, not a file this distribution carries). A gate reading the contract to decide what the decode regime runs would have read a false value: principle 14 from the other direction, an attested claim gone stale under a checkpoint the runtime can finally serve (issue #111). WHICH REGIME THE TABLE SPEAKS: this contract's, not the kernel's. `decode` here is the ONE-ROW forward and `batch` is every M > 1 (contract.CENSUS_PHASE_REGIMES, which says so in its own words); the kernel's `decode` is M <= GEMV_MAX_M and spans eight token counts. The first cut of this entry read the second into the first and published the batch cell WITHOUT the GEMV -- true of the 64-row prefill the census drives, false of the 2-to-8-row forwards the same regime covers, on which the lane serves its own gemv exactly as it does at one row. So tessera_e4m3_k1_dense_sm121_batch_streamed executes BOTH launches, while the decode cell executes the gemv alone, because decode_is_gemv is unconditionally true at one row (the rate-1 refusal starts at the 4-row tile) -- there is no rate condition on a cell anywhere. tests/test_serving_contract.py::test_the_launch_tables_regimes_are_the_routes_own_dispatch derives both regimes from the routes' own decode_is_gemv over every M the dispatch distinguishes, which is what makes this a derivation and not a second guess. WHAT THE VALUE IS DERIVED FROM: tessera.serving.scheme.ROUTE_LAUNCHES, the torch-free table the routes' OWN fp8_gemv.census_expected / bf16_route.census_expected are built from and which owns WINDOW_GEMV_SYMBOL, narrowed by the three axes a cell already carries -- the regime, the residency its TESSERA_SERVE_MODE flag names (both window routes set layer.tessera_gemv = None in resident, so the lane exists in streamed alone), and the lanes each rung REACHES under the predicate native_extensions[].lane.requires publishes (contract v12), which is kernel_window_gemv's own constants. So a cell naming the GEMV cannot outlive the kernel's rate set: change SUPPORTED_RATES and this document stops validating. WHY THE RESIDENCY SPLIT AND NOT A PREDICATE: the two shapes issue #111 offered were a lane predicate on the cell and an explicit rung condition. The rung condition is kept -- rungs_q256 is an enumerated list and a reader resolves no predicate -- but the rung alone cannot separate the two launches, because the one attested E4M3 rung (1024) is lane-readable and the launch there is decided by the residency, which was already a machine-readable cell field spelled as an OR. Two cells of one (platform, family, structure, regime) must now cover DISJOINT residencies, so a reader's answer cannot depend on the order the cells were written in. Cell IDs no longer name a launch: an id is its scope (family, structure, platform, regime, plus the residency where a cell covers only some), because an id that names a launch is a second unparsed spelling of `executes` -- the one that went stale. NOT ADDITIVE, and the schema string says so: a v3 reader must not read a v4 cell, both because `executes` is a key it does not know and because the E4M3 decode answer it would have taken from one cell is now two. TESSERA_BF16_K1 gains `executes` and NO GEMV cell: its attested rung 1792 is root 7, outside SUPPORTED_RATES, so its own streamed GEMV lane is unreachable and the launch a receipt could cover there is the torch window decode under torch.mm -- which is what the derivation returns, unforced. The day a reachable BF16 rung is attested, the same derivation produces its GEMV cell.

MERGE RENUMBER: this landed on a branch that bumped to 11 while another branch bumped to 11 for `construction`; both merged, so one version number named two contracts and this is the later one. native_extensions[].lane: the decoder this extension's OWN lane stamps on a route record (telemetry's 'decoder' field), and -- where the lane has one -- the wire predicate a unit must satisfy before the lane can read it at all. tessera_window_gemv publishes requires.column_rates [1, 2, 4] and requires.window_bits [14], which ARE kernel_window_gemv.SUPPORTED_RATES and WINDOW_BITS_SUPPORTED (tests/test_lane_reachability.py ties the two ends, the way loader_axes is tied to sharding.ROUTE_TP_AXES): that kernel repacks each column's code stream at that column's own rate and has a 16-row lane only where R bits per code is a whole number of bytes, so R = 3 would need 6-byte lanes and is refused. WHY A PRODUCER NEEDS IT: a rung is a ROOT rate and grammar.bresenham_rate_schedule mixes the two rates bracketing it, so q256 1006 (root 3.93) is columns at rate 3 and columns at rate 4, and EVERY unit of such a checkpoint refuses this lane at load -- silently, module by module, through a substitution the route reports as a served module. All six allocated checkpoints held when this was written carried a rate outside the set (docs/measurements/tessera-gemv-lane-reachable-2026-09-03.md section (a), 'The six allocated checkpoints, read from their bytes', names each one and its rate set off the bytes themselves; the checkpoints are build-box artifacts, not files this distribution carries), so no artifact we held could exercise the lane at all, and four censuses that were meant to measure it recorded 112 of 112 modules on torch_window with an empty problem list (issue #104). With the predicate published, a producer refuses the PLAN -- scheme.refuse_unreachable_lane, called at argument time by experiments/export_tessera_serving.py --require-lane, before one unit is encoded -- and a census counts engagement against lane.decoder instead of reading agreement off a fallback it could not see. The NVFP4 entry publishes lane.decoder native_span2 and NO requires block: its eligibility is the route's own, already in formats[], and an empty block would be a claim of no constraint rather than an absence of one (the validator refuses an empty requires for exactly that reason). ADDITIVE in denotation -- no rung, route, range or activation contract moved, and the lane block only states what the kernel already enforced; it is a version bump and not a silent addition because a validating reader refuses a document without lane, which is what contract_version 11 says.

construction: which Linears the runtime offers to a quant config AT ALL, per architecture (#99). Every other block in this contract answers what the plugin EXECUTES; this answers whether it is asked, and the plugin structurally cannot answer that for itself -- LinearBase takes UnquantizedLinearMethod() in the quant_config is None branch without calling get_quant_method, so a module built with quant_config=None is invisible to every quant config that ever existed. On Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration that is EVERY attention projection (MLA at models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py:331, the whole KDA layer at kda.py:171-174, the indexer's wk_weights_proj at attention.py:263) and the whole vision tower (model.py:1082): 20 of 24 Linear patterns, 4 offered. The producer was writing wires into all of them by default, which deletes a weight the runtime wants and declares a module some of those names do not even correspond to -- vLLM builds in_proj_qkvbfg_a and fused_qkv_a_proj where the checkpoint has q/k/v/b/f_a/g_a and q_a/kv_a. The rows are DERIVED from census receipts under docs/measurements/construction/ and re-derived by a test, the same rule native_extensions follows; the census (tools/tessera_construction_census.py) builds the model on the meta device exactly as the loader does, with a probe QuantizationConfig that records every prefix vLLM offers it, so the answer is observed rather than read off source. Two architectures today: Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration on prismaquant/glm53-mia-sm121:487ecf187 and Qwen3ForCausalLM on vllm/vllm-openai:latest (4 of 4 offered -- the control, and the reason this went unseen: every Tessera artifact served so far is Qwen). ADDITIVE for a reader that reads keys by name; a version bump for a reader that validates, because a document without the block is refused, exactly as v7 did for native_extensions. (Landed as v11: #100 took v10 for the serve-image digest pin while this was in flight.)

versions.attested_on.image becomes a DIGEST reference (vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:61fc8a89...) instead of the floating tag vllm/vllm-openai:latest, and that one string is now the serve-image PIN every harness in experiments/ reads through tessera.serving.runtime_image (issue #100). A tag is a name upstream can repoint: two boxes can hold two builds under it while every receipt records the same four words, which is the same defect one level down from the one issue #92 is about. The value is unchanged in what it denotes -- both GB10s were measured on 2026-09-03 to carry exactly this manifest digest -- so nothing that was attested is re-attested here; what changes is that the attestation now NAMES BYTES. Read the pin from this field; it exists nowhere else. NOTE for a reader that compares images: the check is membership in docker's RepoDigests, never .Id, which is the manifest digest under the containerd snapshotter and the config digest under overlay2 -- the same image reads 61fc8a896b0a on one box and 89154ef00dd1 on the other. ADDITIVE for a reader that reads keys by name: the key and its type are unchanged.

native_extensions: the streamed FP8 route's decode-regime GEMV joins the table. The fused window-body GEMV (tessera_window_gemv, built from csrc/window_gemv.cu through tessera.kernel_window_gemv and reached from tessera.serving.fp8_gemv) reads the E4M3 window wire directly at M <= 8, so the library can be resident in a serving process and the import-graph walk refuses a table without it. The module name is exact (that load path carries no build-identity hash), hence the prefix without a trailing separator and the glob that matches the one file it writes. Both residencies substitute the torch window decode without it: streamed serves the same verified bytes through decode + _scaled_mm (slower), and resident never needed it (it decodes once at load through the same torch decoder). A GEMV serve stamps decoder window_gemv on its route record, so the fallback stays visible in a census histogram. ADDITIVE for a reader that reads keys by name: every key a v8 reader read is byte-identical. It is a version bump, not a silent addition, for a reader that validates: a document without the entry is refused, which is what contract_version 9 says -- exactly as v7 did for the block itself.

attested_wire: the wire each attested rung was cut on, beside the rung (#55). attested_rungs_q256 says a receipt covered rung 1792; two encoders can write two byte strings at one rung -- the window table the decoder reads lives on the ALPHABET plane, so anything that moves the table moves the bytes while the rung, the route and the decoder stand still -- and until now the table said nothing about which bytes at 1792 (it mentioned no spread at all). So every formats[] row stamps one wire.recipes entry per attested rung -- the checkpoint's own vocabulary, in the spelling a checkpoint's config already records per rung -- and the validator refuses a stamp that forgets a rung, names one the family does not attest, or carries a body/span/plane the route does not decode (tessera.serving.scheme.ROUTES, the table the loader itself gates on). A producer preflight compares its checkpoint's wire.recipes entry at that rung against the stamp and tells 'attested on these bytes' from 'attested on this rung'. The three stamps are the pinned wire (sigma null everywhere): the v5 BF16 receipt (docs/measurements/tessera-bf16-route-served-2026-09-02.md) and the earlier E2M1x2/E4M3 receipts all predate any reach term, so until the served A/B at R=7 (the #48 gate) re-cuts the attestation on reach-term bytes, the honest reading of the BF16 row is 'route attested at 1792; KL receipt on the pinned wire', and now the table says so itself. The route attestation stands across window-table changes -- the decoder takes the table off the ALPHABET plane and the same kernel decodes the new bytes -- which is why this is a stamp and not a re-attestation. ADDITIVE for a reader that reads keys by name and ignores the ones it does not know: every key a v7 reader read is byte-identical. It is a version bump, not a silent addition, for a reader that validates: a document without attested_wire is refused, which is what contract_version 8 says -- exactly as v4 did for activation_contract.

native_extensions: the libraries this plugin LOADS into a serving process, beside the routes it EXECUTES. The contract published what runs and nothing about what is resident, so a consumer that keys reproducibility on extension residency -- PrismaQuant's serve fingerprint, whose section 7.4 records that a KL is bit-identical inside one container session and drifts 4-8x across them, keyed on whether a lane's .so was resident -- had to mirror the basename into its own pin file. That is principle 14 read backwards: a claim about THIS runtime, maintained in the other repository, where nothing here could refuse it on drift. Until 2026-09-03 that pattern named no Tessera extension at all, so a serve running Tessera's own native span-2 decode fingerprinted identically to a stock serve -- the one lane whose whole point is a custom decoder was the one lane the identical-residency rule could not see. One entry today: the span-2 NVFP4 decoder. It is published as a module_name_prefix and a filename_glob, NOT as a basename, because there is no exact basename to publish -- ext.py JIT-builds the module under a name carrying a build-identity hash, so the library on disk is tessera_nvfp4_<identity>.so and a consumer matching an exact stem would match nothing. match names the rule a gate applies ('basename_fnmatch'), because prose that said 'this is a prefix' is exactly the kind of field principle 14 refuses. The prefix is the constant _load_locked itself passes to cpp_extension.load, and the validator refuses any block that is not tessera.serving.ext.NATIVE_EXTENSIONS, so the table is DERIVED from the load path rather than typed beside it; tests/test_serving_native_extensions.py walks the import graph from tessera.serving and refuses any JIT load site reachable from it that this table does not declare, which is what keeps the list from going quietly short. when_unavailable replaces the 'optional: true' the issue proposed, because optional conflates two facts and answers the wrong one: what a fingerprint needs is not 'absence is survivable' but WHICH serve ran instead, and that differs by residency -- resident substitutes tessera.stock.materialize_stock and stamps decoder 'torch_materialize_stock' on every route record, streamed refuses outright because that path decodes inside a traced forward. So an absent .so with a streamed route record is an impossible pair, which is a stronger check than a boolean allows. The routes gate on this block rather than on a mode comparison of their own (nvfp4_route -> ext.substitutes_when_unavailable), the same way loader_axes is checked against ROUTE_TP_AXES. tessera_window_gemv stays OUT: the criterion is that the library can be resident in a SERVING process, and nothing reachable from tessera.serving loads it -- verified by the import walk, not by reading, so the day a route wires the window GEMV in, the table goes red. ADDITIVE for a reader: a v5 or v6 reader ignores a new top-level key, and no value it already read has moved -- verified, not asserted: PrismaQuant's own contract_answer() over the v6 and v7 payloads is byte-identical.

fused_module: what a vLLM-fused module's roles must SHARE and what is free PER MEMBER, as a value a producer's group allocator reads instead of guessing (#37). The rate is per member. That was always true of the DECODERS -- fp8_route and bf16_route call prepare_window on each role's own body_bits/rates/window_bits and concatenate, nvfp4_route packs each role's own rate/arity/memory/half scalars into that role's row slice -- but nothing published it, and the only place it was written down was the sidecar, which carried ONE q256 per module and refused any member that disagreed with it. So the exporter grouped a fused module on (grid, q256) equality and passed a mixed-rung group through at source precision, while PrismaQuant's group knapsack (fold ON by default) allocates exactly such groups: two halves of one pipeline describing different sets. The sidecar now spells a mixed group as a per-role q256 list (sidecar_q256), every role's rung goes through the same reader-range gate the module's one rung used to, and each member is compared against its own declared rate at parse. ADDITIVE for readers: formats[], lane_eligibility, tensor_parallel, expert_parallel and quant_method are byte-identical to v5, so a v5 reader that ignores unknown top-level keys gets exactly the answers it got before; what it must NOT do is assume q256 is scalar, and a pre-v6 PLUGIN does not -- it refuses the list form rather than mis-reading it. mixed_rung_receipt is false: the relaxation is proven by a decode identity on a real Qwen3-0.6B q/k/v at rungs 1024/900/1200 (element-for-element against the same roles decoded alone and against tessera.decode.materialize_fp8/materialize_bf16), not by a vLLM serve, and no lane_eligibility cell moved. NVFP4 is unaffected in practice: TESSERA_E2M1_K2 publishes the single point 896, so every member of an NVFP4 group lands on one rung anyway and the gate that says so is the reader range, not a rule about groups.

TESSERA_BF16_K1 stops being unattested. v4 gave its formats[] row an activation_contract, which says what the route EXECUTES; this says a receipt COVERED it, and the two are different claims: attested_rungs_q256 [1792] (R=7, the rung the receipt served) and two sm_121 dense cells, decode and batch, both bf16_unquantized on torch.mm with the row scale as an fp32 epilogue. The receipt is docs/measurements/tessera-bf16-route-served-2026-09-02.md: four route censuses on the pinned image -- resident/eager, resident/compiled, streamed/eager, streamed/compiled -- each recording all 112 declared modules on the TESSERA_BF16 route with decoder torch_window in BOTH the prefill and the decode shape and zero problems, plus a served KL-vs-BF16 in both residency modes on the Qwen-tokenized n=8 x 512 corpus against the image-matched teacher, with the folded stock twin on vanilla vLLM as the control. route_status is backed_with_serve_flag because the residency is selected by TESSERA_SERVE_MODE and both values were served; qualification is device_qualified because the censuses ran on this GB10 (sm_121, capability [12, 1]), not on a table. Nothing wider is attested: one rung, one platform, dense structure only, no routed-MoE cell, and tensor_parallel.units still caps this family at max_world_size 1.

formats[] rows gain activation_contract: the A-side contract the route for that family EXECUTES, as a value a gate can read. It was published only on lane_eligibility cells, so a family with no cell yet -- exactly TESSERA_BF16_K1, whose v3 entry landed unattested -- published its activation contract in changelog PROSE and nowhere a gate could reach, which is the principle-14 failure that field exists to prevent: a consumer could not tell 'unquantised by design' from 'nobody filled it in'. PrismaQuant's lane preflight found it within the hour, deriving an executes glob for a family whose A side it could not price. The value is checked against tessera.serving.scheme.ROUTES[route]['activation_contract'] -- the dict the routes themselves dispatch on -- exactly as loader_axes is checked against ROUTE_TP_AXES, so the document and the code cannot drift; and every cell's activation_contract must equal its family's row, so the two places that carry it cannot disagree. The A side is a claim about execution, not about attestation: the row says what the decoder feeds the GEMM, the cell says a receipt covered it, and TESSERA_BF16_K1 now honestly publishes bf16_unquantized with attested_rungs_q256 still empty. ADDITIVE: a v3 reader ignores the new field, and the cells it already read are unchanged.

tensor_parallel.units[] gains loader_axes: per axis, what this build's LOADER does with a shard on it ('sharded' or 'refused', plus a prose reason a gate does not read). The seam that cuts a unit landed (tessera.layout.slice_unit + serving/sharding), and the plugin's config gate had gone on refusing every tensor_parallel_size > 1 with a message saying the cutter was not in the build -- narrower than the code and, by then, false. The gate is now keyed on the slicer's PRESENCE, and the per-axis refusal moved to create_weights where the axis is known: TESSERA_E4M3_K1 cuts both axes (the window body's L-bit pad IS state_{-1}), TESSERA_E2M1_K2 cuts columns only (its span-2 TCQ decoders supply state_{-1} = 0 themselves). max_world_size is UNCHANGED at 1 and keeps its meaning -- the largest world size a served receipt covers -- because no multi-rank serve has been run; raising it needs a two-rank serve with a per-rank census and a KL against the single-rank arm, not a passing unit test. The validator no longer refuses a world size above one with the claim that a sharded form needs per-rank wires: it does not, the artifact is TP-agnostic and the cut happens at load. ADDITIVE -- a v1 reader that reads max_world_size still gets 1, which is the conservative answer. Third family: TESSERA_BF16_K1, the scalar BF16 grid over the CHANNEL plane and the same window body the E4M3 family ships, decoded to a plain bf16 tile and served W16A16 through the stock BF16 GEMM (activation contract bf16_unquantized -- a value, because a gate must be able to tell 'unquantised by design' from 'nobody filled it in'). It exists because the E4M3 ALPHABET floors the window body at ~0.022 out-space from R=6 upward while the identical trellis over bf16 keeps halving at ~1.93x per bit, so above ~6 bpp an 8-bit tile has nothing left to buy. reader_rate_range_q256 is [256, 4096] continuous at step 1, DERIVED the way E4M3's was in v2 -- 25 candidate rungs (every integer rate 1..16 plus nine non-integer rungs of the kind a Bresenham schedule makes: 300, 777, 779, 1000, 1023, 1500, 2047, 2500, 4095) encoded and taken through the route's own load path, parse -> shard -> prepare including the element-for-element cross-check against tessera.decode.materialize_bf16 (experiments/bf16_reader_rate_range.py). 4096 is the grammar's shaped domain (code rate 1..16 over a 16-bit alphabet) and the sweep reaches it: the recipe widens the window table to max(14, rate) above R=14 rather than refusing, and L=15 and L=16 both load. The only candidate refused was q256=777 over 128 columns, and that is a GEOMETRY refusal ('it needs 9/2 columns at rate 4') not a rate one -- it loads at 512 columns, so it does not bound the range. attested_rungs_q256 is EMPTY and there is no lane_eligibility cell: no container receipt covers this family yet -- no served census and no served KL against the plain-BF16 twin the exporter writes -- so every BF16 rung resolves unattested, which is the honest status and not a refusal. A cell is added when a receipt exists. Additive: a v1/v2 reader that does not know this family simply does not match it. tensor_parallel gains a TESSERA_BF16_K1 unit with the same loader_axes as TESSERA_E4M3_K1 -- both cut, because the axis answer is a property of the window BODY (its L-bit pad IS state_{-1}) and this family ships that body over the same CHANNEL plane; its create_weights calls the same require_axis_supported gate. max_world_size is 1 like the others: no multi-rank serve has been run.

reader_rate_range_q256 now states what the DECODER accepts, measured by encoding a unit at each candidate rate and running it through the route's own load path; the plugin refuses a declared q256 outside it (it did not before, and an allocated checkpoint carrying seven unlisted rungs served with nothing refusing). E4M3 widened from [1024,1024] to [256,2048] continuous at step 1 -- the bound is the trellis grammar's shaped domain (code rate 1..8 over an 8-bit-native alphabet), not the rungs anyone had exported. E2M1x2 stays the single point 896, bounded BELOW by the native decoder (span-2 TCQ only; the sub-cap WINDOW body has no served decode) and ABOVE by the same grammar (rate 7 of arity-2 native 8). candidate_rungs_q256 renamed attested_rungs_q256 because it never was the decodable set and reading it as one is how the gap opened: it is the rungs a lane_eligibility cell attests. Added an explicit grid to each entry so a (route, grid) pair with no published range refuses rather than resolving to another entry's numbers. candidate_rungs_q256 is retained as a DEPRECATED ALIAS of attested_rungs_q256 -- same list, refused if it disagrees -- so this stays an ADDITIVE change that a v1 reader can still read, which is why the schema string does not move. It is dropped at schema v2.
First published contract: two dense families, four cells, TP1/EP0.
